summary: Hisao Inagaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1949–1953) and the University of London (~1966–1968). He held a post at SOAS University of London (1970) and served as Professor at Ryukoku University (~1981–1998).
Hisao Kanaseki worked in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied at Doshisha University (~1938–1941) and held a post at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1963–1982).

Hisao Takahashi, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, completed doctoral studies at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano. He held posts at Taisho University (attested 1977–2010, including professor) and the Buzan-ha Institute of Modern Mission (attested 1995).
Hisashi Matsumura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at the Australian National University (attested 1982) and Kobe Shinwa University (attested 1996).

Hisashi Sato was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology who studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936). He served as Professor at Kyoto University (~1964–1977), Komazawa University, and Toyo University, and held a post at Bukkyo University (~1977).

Hisataka Ishida works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna in 2011 under Helmut Krasser, among other teachers, and held a lecturer post at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2015).
Hitoshi Inui is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kanjin Horiuchi. He held teaching posts at Koyasan University, where he was attested as lecturer (1986–1992) and professor (2015).

Hitoshi Katō works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. In 1992, he held posts at Otani University, Osaka University of Foreign Studies, and Nara University of Education, later serving as professor at Osaka University (attested 2016–2017).

Hitoshi Obara works in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Hokkaido University (~1963–1967) and served as a professor at the University of the Sacred Heart (~1990–2015).

Hjalmar Edgren was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln and under William Dwight Whitney. He held posts at Lund University (~1880–1885), the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (~1885–1901), and the University of Gothenburg (~1891–1893).
Hla Pe was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the University of Yangon (~1931–1935) and the University of London (~1938–1944).
Ho-chin Yang is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Yang completed a PhD at the University of Washington in 1994 under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.
Ho-sung Kim works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Kim founded the Institute for the History of Japanese Buddhism and held a professorship at Dongguk University (attested 2011).

Hojun Nagasaki is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1963–1965). He served at Otani University (~1968–1999) as professor and professor emeritus, and presided over the Japanese Association for Jain Studies (1998).

Holly Gayley is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She was a doctoral candidate at Harvard University (~2001–2009) and took up a post at the University of Colorado Boulder (~2008).

Hong Luo works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Luo completed doctoral studies at Peking University and held posts at the China Tibetology Research Center and Sichuan University as professor.

Honsho Ueda is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Minobusan Junior College as lecturer (attested 1963) and professor (attested 1992), and later served as a professor at Minobusan University (attested 1996–2001).
Hoong Teik Toh is a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Harvard University in 2004, studying under Gray Tuttle, Ruohong Li, Hongmei Jin, and Yudru Tsomu.

Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales was an archaeology, history, and Indology scholar. Educated at Charterhouse School (~1914–1918) and Queens' College, Cambridge (~1919–1922), he served as Field Director for the Greater India Research Committee (~1934–1941).

Horace Hayman Wilson was an Indologist. He held posts at the East India Company, the India Government Mint in Kolkata (1816–1833), the University of Oxford as Boden Professor (1833–1836), and the Royal Asiatic Society as Director (1837).
